display_name: Encoding of the Courts Law provisions Amendment No. 105 touches or the Basic Law cites (ss 2, 2A, 6, 6B, 6C, 7(b), 7(c), 8, 14, 25), both vintages

run.agent: a Sonnet 5.5 encoder working for the lead of session israel
run.method: one agent, one session, no sub-agents, from the lead's brief; the rules read from the page images of the amending instruments

language.note: Identifiers and comments are English. Hebrew is quoted only in comments, copied from the consolidation or the instrument named in the comment; text read from a page image is marked so.

seat: the individual the Courts Law's rules are applied to: a candidate for the Supreme Court, a person whom the Knesset might choose as a public representative on the committee, and a judge whose term the committee is asked to end; the committee, the Minister of Justice, the Knesset and the Court have no seat

source.authority: aid: unofficial Hebrew Wikisource consolidation, as amended at retrieval

other_sources.what: Courts Law [Consolidated Version] (Amendment No. 105), Sefer HaChukim 3389, 1 April 2025, pp. 438-440: s 1 (s 2A), s 2 (s 6), s 3 (new ss 6B, 6C), s 4 (s 7), s 5 (s 8(a)), s 6 (s 25), s 7 (indirect amendment of the Knesset Law), s 8 (commencement and application)
other_sources.authority: official publication (the Knesset's PDF of Sefer HaChukim), read from the page images

scope: Encoded: the provisions Amendment No. 105 touches, namely ss 2A, 6 (with its definitions of the coalition and opposition factions), 6B, 6C, 7(b) and (c) (7(c) repealed from the 26th Knesset), 8(a) and 25(b), in two vintages where the text differs; and two provisions it does not touch, s 2 (cited by 6C(a) and 25(b)) and s 14(b), (c) (the procedure for ending a term under Basic Law s 7(4), which row IL-37 encodes); the cross-references as typed values. Every other section is out of scope: not touched by the amendment and not needed by a provision it touches. The indirect amendment of the Knesset Law (Amendment No. 105 s 7) is not encoded.

not_reviewed.note: No domain expert has read this encoding against the source, and no independent tester has run. Every expected value in the tests modules was worked by hand from the Hebrew text of the instrument before it was asserted; a mutation check on scratch copies shows the tests can fail.
